questions.question: What are the possible states of a time card in ServiceNow Time Card Management?

options.text: Pending, Submitted, Approved, Processed, Rejected, Recalled

explanation.correct: Time cards can have six states: Pending (not submitted), Submitted (submitted for approval), Approved, Processed (approved with expense line created), Rejected, and Recalled (approved card returned for adjustments).

wrongAnswers.explanation: These are not the correct time card states
These are generic task states, not time card specific states
These are not the correct time card states

source.excerpt: A time card can have any of the following states: Pending, Submitted, Approved, Processed, Rejected, Recalled.

questions.question: What task types does the time card management feature work with? (Choose FOUR)

explanation.correct: The time card management feature works with the Task table to record time worked on Projects, Incidents, Problems, and Change Requests. Knowledge Articles and Service Catalog Items are not task types that support time card entry.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Knowledge Articles are documentation, not tasks that support time card entry
Service Catalog Items are request types, not tasks that support time card entry directly

source.excerpt: The time card management feature works with the Task table to record time worked on Projects, Incidents, Problems, and Change Requests.

questions.question: What happens when you approve a time card in ServiceNow?

options.text: The time card is deleted and hours are transferred to the task
The time logged is saved day-wise in the Time Card Daily table
A notification is sent to the submitter only
The time card is automatically closed

explanation.correct: When you approve a time card, the time logged in the time card is saved day-wise in the Time Card Daily [time_card_daily] table. This enables generating time card reports by days for any period irrespective of the time sheet period.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Time cards are not deleted upon approval; they are retained with the Approved state
While notifications may be sent, the key action is saving daily time data
Approved time cards move to Approved state, not automatically closed

source.excerpt: When you approve a time card, the time logged in the time card is saved day-wise in the Time Card Daily [time_card_daily] table.

questions.question: Which actions can a time card approver perform on submitted time sheets? (Choose THREE)

options.text: Recall the time sheet for corrections
Reassign the time sheet to a different resource

explanation.correct: Time card approvers can review, approve, reject, or recall submitted time sheets for corrections.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Approvers cannot permanently delete time sheets; they can only approve, reject, or recall them
Reassigning time sheets to different resources is not an approver action

source.excerpt: Time card approvers can review, approve, reject, or recall submitted time sheets for corrections.

questions.question: What limitation exists when a time card approver delegates their approval tasks?

options.text: They cannot delegate to users outside their department
They cannot limit delegation to individual resources
They can only delegate for a maximum of 30 days
They must get admin approval before delegating

explanation.correct: Approvers can delegate their approval tasks, but cannot limit delegation to individual resources. The delegation applies to all time card approvals assigned to them.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no department restriction mentioned for delegation
There is no 30-day maximum mentioned for delegation
Admin approval is not required for delegating time card approval tasks

source.excerpt: Approvers can delegate their approval tasks, but cannot limit delegation to individual resources.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow table does Time Card Management work with to record time worked on tasks?

explanation.correct: Time Card Management works with the Task table to record time worked on various task types, such as projects, incidents, problems, and change requests.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Time Entry is not the core table that Time Card Management integrates with; it works with the Task table
While Project Tasks extend the Task table, Time Card Management works with the base Task table to support multiple task types
Time Sheet is a Time Card Management artifact, not the table it works with for task tracking

source.excerpt: Time Card Management works with the Task table to record time worked on various task types, such as projects, incidents, problems, and change requests.

questions.question: On which mobile platforms can users access and manage time sheets using the ServiceNow Mobile Timesheets app?

explanation.correct: Users can access and manage time sheets through the ServiceNow Mobile Timesheets app on iOS and Android devices.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Mobile Timesheets app is available on both iOS and Android, not just iOS
The Mobile Timesheets app is available on both iOS and Android, not just Android
Windows Mobile is not mentioned as a supported platform for the Mobile Timesheets app

source.excerpt: Users can access and manage time sheets through the ServiceNow Mobile Timesheets app on iOS and Android devices.

questions.question: What role is required to approve timecards submitted by team members?

explanation.correct: The it_project_manager role is used to approve timecards for project tasks. Project managers approve time entries submitted against their projects.

wrongAnswers.explanation: timecard_admin manages timecard configuration, not individual approvals
project_manager is not the specific ServiceNow role name used
resource_manager manages allocations, not timecard approvals
